label: rem:swampland-island-of-consistency
title: Swampland correspondence: Bring rigidity and the island of consistency
html:
Bring's surface enters the framework as a rigid selection. Its categorical Euler characteristic is fixed:

  \chi(A) = -6

is the genus-4 curve that realises this value. This rigidity provides the QOU counterpart to the Swampland "island of consistency".

The Swampland statement. Within the landscape of effective field theories, only a sparse subset admits a quantum-gravity completion [vafa2005]. Consistency criteria such as the Weak Gravity Conjecture [arkani-hamed2007] carve out the admissible region. This leaves isolated islands rather than a continuum.

QOU translation. Demanding an observable volume fixes the categorical Euler characteristic to \chi(A) = -6. The genus-4 hyperbolic structure realising this value is rigid. By Mostow rigidity, a finite-volume hyperbolic structure of dimension at least three admits no continuous deformation. Therefore, the topological data and the masses derived from it are discrete. The framework occupies an isolated point rather than a continuous family of vacua.

Scope. The derivation of \chi(A) = -6 is Lean-checked. The identification of Bring's surface as the terminal genus-4 object is a categorical result. The stronger reading—that this geometric rigidity selects the substrate parameter q_0—is motivational, not derived. Calibration against the muon-to-electron mass ratio fixes q_0, not Mostow rigidity. No theorem established here forces q_0 from \chi(A) = -6. Mostow rigidity makes the hyperbolic geometry discrete. It does not, on its own, determine the substrate modulus.
